title: Equivalence of the two definitions of total variation distance
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$. Then the total variation distance $\mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u) = 	frac{1}{2}
orm{\mu-
u}_{\mathrm{TV}}$, defined as half the total variation norm of the signed measure $\mu-
u$, agrees with its supremum form over events,
\[
  \mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u) \;=\; \sup igl\{\,\abs{\mu(S)-
u(S)} : S \subseteq \Omega 	ext{ measurable}\, igr\}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ is a probability measure on Ω
ν is a probability measure on Ω
replaced:
The total-variation-mass definition and the supremum-over-events definition coincide:
$\mathrm{TV}(\mu,\nu) = \mathrm{TV}_{\sup}(\mu,\nu)$.
